chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya' ibn Ya'qub from 'Ali' ibn Ibraheem from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Muhammad' ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl from Safwan and Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, he said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not neglect visiting all the shrines: Masjid Quba, for it is the mosque which was "founded on piety from the first day"; and Mashrabah of Umm Ibrahim (peace be upon him); and Masjid al-Fadikh; and the graves of the martyrs; and Masjid al-Ahzab, which is Masjid al-Fath.'

He said: 'And we have reached that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when he visited the graves of the martyrs would say: "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; excellent is the final abode."'

And let what you say at Masjid al-Fath be: "O Cryer of the distressed, and O Responder to the supplication of the needy, remove my anxiety, my sorrow, and my distress, just as You removed from Your Prophet his anxiety, his sorrow, and his distress, and protected him from the terror of his enemy in this place."

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ اَلْفَتْحِ: Masjid al-Fath, also known as Masjid al-Ahzab
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ اَلْفَضِيخِ: Masjid al-Fadikh, a mosque in Medina
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ قُبَاءَ: Masjid Quba, the first mosque built by the Prophet
key_terms.مَشْرَبَةُ أُمِّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Mashrabah of Umm Ibrahim, a sacred site

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended shrines to visit in Medina and the supplications associated with them according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual hierarchy of Medina’s sacred sites, elevating Masjid Quba as the prototype of piety based on its Quranic foundation. It prescribes specific supplications for these locations, linking the patience of martyrs to the intercessory power of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) at Masjid al-Fath, thereby integrating historical events with devotional practice in Shia tradition.
